overview: This table sets up a Story mode battle by choosing its map, waves, intro, results screen, and how easily it earns a high rank.
description: Defines a story battle mission: map, wave chain and flags controlling appearance, result screen and score scaling.

ID.simple: The unique name of this Story mode mission. The game uses it to connect the mission to its story scene, saved progress, and tutorial steps.
ID.technical: FName native Id and the export ImportKeyField/row key; all 90 exported rows have key == Id. Launch normally reaches the row through StoryDemo.Id_StoryMission: Story_ResolveDemoLaunch writes that id to FStudioPhaseRequest.Name34, which GamePhase copies to GameManager.StudioStoryMissionId_CE0. Story_FindMissionRow and the out-of-line finders then search StoryMissionDataTables (DTM +0x8D0). The same id keys StudioMissionRecords_680 on a story win, and Story_GetFreeMissions compares it with Demo.Id_StoryMission. Suffix M is classified as a main mission by telemetry/UI code; the tutorial row STMSN_01000M is also hard-coded in battle/tutorial logic.

Id_Map.simple: Chooses the battlefield and the map picture shown in character selection. If left empty, the game chooses an available battlefield at random.
Id_Map.technical: FName (row +0x10). Story_GetMissionMapId and the inline ternary in Story_ResolveDemoLaunch use this id when it is not NAME_None; otherwise (including a null mission row in the helper) Story_PickRandomMapId_12FD510 picks a uniformly random Map row whose MapSelectPlacementIndex >= 0. The chosen id is written to the battle request, and when the demo has no pre-battle script the matching Map row FileName list supplies the loaded levels. Character-select code also reads the raw id for the map thumbnail and can dereference an unguarded Map lookup. All 90 exports set a map id (18 distinct keys that all resolve in MapDataTable; none is None), although three of those map rows have MapSelectPlacementIndex -1 and therefore would not be candidates for the random fallback.

Id_StoryMissionWave.simple: Lists the waves of allies and enemies in the order they appear, usually just one. The first wave helps decide who the player controls and which companions join them.
Id_StoryMissionWave.technical: TArray<FName> (row +0x18). Every export has four slots: 89 use slot 0 and leave slots 1-3 None; STMSN_09112M uses four valid ids. All 93 referenced ids resolve in StoryMissionWaveDataTable. Slot 0 supplies the first wave used for PlayableCharacterIndex, allies, MissionWave/task and battle-talk lookups. Several launch and select paths dereference GetData()[0] or [0] without a Num check; Story_FindFirstWave and the battle notify helpers do check. The mission retry count indexes this array for later waves; Story_GetBattleLayout returns 255 for a null row, out-of-range index or missing wave/MissionWave row and maps tabulated ally/enemy counts to EGameBattlePair values 0-11 (unsupported counts leave 0). Story_GetMissionAllyCharacters resolves None slots by failed lookup rather than an explicit filter, skips them, stops after the first successful wave when bAllWaves is false, and walks every slot only when bAllWaves is true.

bAppearanceDisabled.simple: Skips the opening character introduction the first time this mission is played. On retries, that introduction is already skipped.
bAppearanceDisabled.technical: bool (row +0x28), constructor default false. AGameBattleManager::IsAppearanceEnabled returns (flag != 1) only when RetryCount <= 0 and a StoryMission row is cached; any retry returns false regardless of the flag, while a missing story row returns true on the first attempt. The intro state jumps to step 10 when the result is false. This reconstruction traces the cache write from GamePhase_BattleStory::SetupBattleCharacterEntries through AGameBattleManager::SetupStoryMission into FStudioBattleMissionTaskSystem::SetupStory (System360) and FStudioBattleSystem390::SetStoryMission. 49/90 exported rows set true.

bResultDisabled.simple: Skips the normal results screen when the player wins the final wave. Losses and earlier waves still follow the normal battle flow.
bResultDisabled.technical: bool (row +0x29), constructor default false. In FBattleStoryState_Finish::RequestState this is checked only after HasNextMissionWave() is false and GetWinnerTeam() == 0 (Team A win). When true, the game calls OnBattleFinished/OnBattleWon and sets BattleEndRequest = 0 instead of requesting the normal result state. Losses, non-final waves and false rows follow the normal path. 40/90 exported rows set true.

ResultEvaluationScoreRate.simple: Changes how much the battle score counts toward the rank shown after a Story mission. Higher values make the same score more likely to earn a better rank.
ResultEvaluationScoreRate.technical: float (row +0x2C), constructor default 0.0f. GetResultEvaluationScoreRate starts at 1.0f, replaces it with StoryMission->ResultEvaluationScoreRate when System360 has a story row, then lets ArcadeMission->ResultEvaluationScoreRate override it whenever that cache is also set. The result snapshot builder uses the same precedence: it converts float(Value43C) * rate to int32 (truncation toward zero) and passes the score to GetResultScoreRank; that block runs only when PlayerCharacter is valid and BonusEntries has an entry for the character index. The PvE result state also passes GetResultEvaluationScoreRate() to GetBonusScoreRank to raise MissionWaveRank. Exported rates are 1.0 (83 rows), 1.2 (5), 1.5 (1) and 2.0 (1); no row omits the field.

notes: The reconstructed struct constructor sets both bools false and the rate 0.0f; all 90 exported rows explicitly supply all six values. A row that actually reached either score consumer with the constructor 0.0f would yield score 0; the serialization behavior for a missing field was not independently tested.

The battle row cache is traced here: GamePhase_BattleStory::SetupBattleCharacterEntries (0x102a560 area) -> AGameBattleManager::SetupStoryMission -> FStudioBattleMissionTaskSystem::SetupStory and FStudioBattleSystem390::SetStoryMission. The remaining NEED-PROBE comment on GameBattleSystems_B.h:201 is stale relative to those reconstructed writers; no runtime launch was used to re-observe it.

Export check across every JSON file in JJKCCDatatables: one StoryMissionDataTable (90 rows, no numbered shard, localization variant, or per-character copy), 90/90 row key == Id, 68 M and 22 S ids, 18 valid MapDataTable references, 93/93 StoryMissionWaveDataTable references, and 89/90 mission ids referenced by a StoryDemo (STMSN_06090S is unreferenced). In every matched demo reference the StoryDemo row name equals the mission id.

Array/order precedence: slot 0 is the first wave, and the mission retry count selects later wave entries; Story_GetBattleLayout bounds-checks that index and returns 255 on invalid/missing rows. Several select and launch paths still read slot 0 unguarded. A non-None Id_Map wins over random selection, Arcade score rate wins over Story score rate, a pending next wave wins over bResultDisabled, and retries always win over bAppearanceDisabled.

Behavior marked verified is static retail-aligned reconstruction in C++ (retail RVAs/finder addresses are recorded in the source comments), not a separate retail Blueprint inspection. No retail Blueprint logic or live game/editor trace was available for this review; project guidance states shipped gameplay behavior is in C++.

usages.detail: Loads the sole exported table into StoryMissionDataTables (DTM +0x8D0).
Story_ResolveDemoLaunch copies Demo.Id_StoryMission into FStudioPhaseRequest.Name34; GamePhase.cpp:218 copies it to GM+0xCE0.
Launch looks up the mission from StoryDemo.Id_StoryMission and reads its first wave.
Id_Map is used directly unless None, in which case an eligible random Map id is selected; line 487 uses the map FileName list as levels.
First-wave and playable-ally chain dereferences Id_StoryMissionWave[0] without a Num check.
Story_GetMissionAllyCharacters uses one wave or every wave according to bAllWaves.
Story_GetBattleLayout maps the indexed wave ally/enemy counts to a battle pair, with 255 for invalid/missing data.
Battle setup dereferences the mission and wave chain; line 202 passes the row to the battle manager.
SetupStoryMission caches the row in System360 and System390.
System390 special-cases Id == STMSN_01000M for tutorial brain changes; line 1328 initializes tutorial steps from the id.
A win writes progress into StudioMissionRecords_680 keyed by StudioStoryMissionId_CE0.
IsAppearanceEnabled applies bAppearanceDisabled only before the first retry.
bResultDisabled short-circuits the result phase only after the last wave on a Team A win.
Story rate (then Arcade override) scales Value43C before the story result rank lookup.
PvE result uses GetResultEvaluationScoreRate indirectly for bonus rank.
Telemetry classifies Mission.Id ending in M as main and other ids as side missions.
Free-mission filtering compares StoryDemo.Id_StoryMission to Mission.Id.
Mission Id_Map selects the map icon; GamePhase_StoryCharacterSelect.cpp:396 uses the helper with random fallback for battle settings.
